page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance utilizes a dedicated Intel processor featuring 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. The hardware supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) for accelerated matrix operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but weak to poor multi-core and memory throughput. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1554.59 (average), and Geekbench single-core reaches 1640.0 (average). However, multi-core performance is limited, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1600.79 (poor) and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2036.0 (weak). Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 132.41 GB/sec for cached small blocks and dropping to 15.05 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. Database operations and Redis SET performance are rated as poor, with Redis achieving 2.24 million operations per second.

With a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, the n4-highmem-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions provides specialized hardware acceleration for lightweight vector and integer operations, though the dual-thread single-core design limits heavy multi-threaded tasks. This instance is best suited for small-scale memory-intensive applications, basic text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, and lightweight caching layers where memory capacity is prioritized over raw compute throughput.
